title: New r2 comments re-assert the r1-flagged imprecise mechanism: 'ctx.state snapshot taken at construction' — ADK 2.2.0 ctx.state wraps the live session.state dict by reference, not a copy
evidence:
tenant_scorer/agent.py:594-597:
            # Read the judge's output_key off the RAW session dict, NOT
            # ctx.state: a child's output_key write is merged into the live
            # session.state (visible via ctx.session.state) but is absent
            # from this node's ctx.state snapshot taken at construction —

ADK source (installed 2.2.0, google/adk/agents/context.py:181-184):
    self._state = State(
        value=invocation_context.session.state,
        delta=self._event_actions.state_delta,
detail: ctx.state is not a copy: Context.__init__ wraps the live session.state dict by reference (State.__init__ sets _value=value), so child writes stay visible under InMemory. The None-read divergence arises only when the session service reassigns session.state mid-run. Same mechanism overstatement r1 noted, re-added in new r2 comment lines.
recommended_fix: Reword to: 'ctx.state._value references the session.state dict captured at construction; if the session service reassigns session.state during a child run_node, the reference goes stale while ctx.session.state re-reads the live attribute.'
